docs.text: The Coast Guard issued a warning for boaters and beachgoers at Lake Michigan in the Milwaukee area to steer clear of any strange cylinders after three canisters of phosphorous pyrotechnics failed to activate and were lost during a recent joint military exercise with the Air Force.
The U.S. Coast Guard warned Lake Michigan beachgoers Tuesday to be cautious of three missing phosphorus pyrotechnics after one washed up on Montrose Beach on Monday.

The U.S. Coast Guard warned Lake Michigan boaters and beachgoers about three missing phosphorous pyrotechnics leftover from a joint military exercise with the Coast Guard and Air Force that occurred earlier this month offshore of Milwaukee.

Safety Notice for Lake Michigan Visitors
The U.S. Coast Guard has issued a warning about three unaccounted phosphorous pyrotechnics in Lake Michigan after a recent training exercise near Milwaukee. If you spot a silver cylinder on the beach or in the water, keep your distance and call 911.
